InstitutionalDepartmentName: Institute of Cognitive Neurology and Dementia Research (IKND)
TaskDescription: Passive viewing with an orthogonal target-detection task. Object images were shown centrally at 7 degrees visual angle on a grey background with a white fixation cross superimposed, each for 500 ms, followed by an inter-stimulus interval drawn at random from 250-450 ms in 50 ms steps (mean 350 ms). 96 objects were presented per session, 48 of which the participant had trained on and 48 of which they had not. A session comprised 15 runs of about 263 s; within each run all 96 objects appeared twice in random order, never twice in immediate succession, giving 30 repetitions of each object per session. Every 4 to 6 object presentations a target image (a hammer) appeared for 500 ms, to which participants responded with a button press; it was followed by an extended 1500 ms inter-stimulus interval so that blinks and motor artefacts did not contaminate the next trial. Those button presses are recorded in events.tsv as response events and are the only behavioural measure collected in the scanner.
Instructions: Participants were asked to attend to each object image while keeping their gaze on the central fixation cross, and to press a button whenever the target image (a hammer) appeared. They were told they could blink during the longer interval that followed each target. No response was required to the object images themselves.
